_source: Ministry of Education / Curriculum Development Centre, Zambia. 'Grade 10-12 Geography Syllabus' (2013, published by CDC), Section D (Zambia) — all of Grade 12. Topic/sub-topic names and Specific Outcome statements only; the 'Content' (Knowledge/Skills/Values) columns are omitted for the same column-extraction-reliability reason documented in the Grade 10 file. Outcome text and order were manually traced against each sub-topic heading, cross-checked against the syllabus's own end-of-document 'Scope and Sequence Chart' summary table, which confirmed every topic name and the full topic list used here. Two numbering slips found in the source document itself were corrected based on the outcome's position under its true sub-topic rather than its printed code: the outcome about invasive plant species is printed as '12.2.1.3' but is renumbered 12.2.2.1 here (it is clearly about sub-topic 12.2.2 'Invasive Plant Species', not 12.2.1 'Exploitation of Timber'); the outcome about interpreting mining production/marketing data tables is printed as '12.4.2.2' but is renumbered 12.5.2.1 here (it is clearly about sub-topic 12.5.2 'Mineral Production', not Topic 12.4 'Wildlife and Tourism'). Two further outcomes were printed with a truncated code ('.10.1.1') in the source, most likely a garbled '12.10.1.1' / '12.12.2.1' — renumbered here to 12.10.1.1 and 12.12.2.1 respectively based on their sub-topic position. Topic 12.3 does not exist in the source document — its numbering jumps directly from 12.2 (Forestry) to 12.4 (Wildlife and Tourism), confirmed by the Scope and Sequence Chart, which also skips straight from Forestry to Wildlife; this is a genuine gap in the original syllabus, not an extraction artifact. The syllabus organizes content by Grade only, not by Term, so all of Grade 12 is modeled as a single term here.

curriculum.description: Zambia's 2013 outcome-based curriculum for Grades 10-12 (Senior Secondary).

subject.name: Geography

competencies.description: Describe land tenure
State types of land tenure in Zambia
State factors that favour irrigation farming
Describe effects of irrigation farming on the environment
Explain bad agricultural practices and their effects
Discuss soil conservation measures and sustainable agriculture
Explain Zambia's agricultural potential in the SADC region
Describe factors limiting the commercial exploitation of indigenous trees
Describe the problems affecting forests
Explain effects of invasive plant species (Lantana camara, Kafue weed)

topics.name: 12.4 Wildlife in Zambia

competencies.description: Explain the importance of wildlife
Identify factors that hinder the growth of the wildlife and tourism industry
Identify government measures put in place to promote wildlife conservation and the tourism industry
State factors influencing exploitation of minerals
Interpret simple tables of data showing production and marketing figures of mining companies

sub_topics.name: 12.7.2 Uses of Hydro-Electric Power and its Effects in Zambia

competencies.description: State prospects for landlocked countries
